messages.subject: Goodness of fit of IRT models
messages.subject_clean: Goodness of fit of IRT models
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Philip and MIRT community,

My name is Parth Soni and I am a PhD student from India. I am working on a project where I intend to estimate students' growth in math. I am analysing the test response data using the "mirt" package and I have some questions about the goodness of fit statistics for IRT models.

The tests contain 15 to 20 multiple choice questions. Four tests were conducted within an academic year for maths. I have the dichotomous response patterns for each student. Students are from grades 3 to 5 and sample size varies between 300 to 600 on all tests. My questions are as under:

(i) While analysing tests, if I check for M2 statistics, some tests fit 2PL while others fit 3PL, and in some cases none of the two fits. I understand that using 2PL or 3PL is to be considered based upon the intent and application of the test. In my data, I have found that pseudo-guessing parameters for many items are higher, some being higher than even 0.5. Hence, I decided to use the 3PL model. But, since it does not fit, would you suggest removing some items with extreme difficulty or pseudo-guessing parameters? Should I proceed ahead even when M2 shows misfit?

(ii) Some literature suggests that testing for the goodness of fit of "items" are more important than the whole test. When I check for S-X2 (summated chi-square) in mirt, almost all items show proper fit. But still the overall test does not fit the 2PL model. Do you suggest that testing for item fit would be sufficient?

(iii) In most of the cases where I test for 3PL, the model does not converge. One of the books suggests that we can specify the range of pseudo-guessing parameters and fix that model in the "mirt" function instead of using "model=1". See the code below:
spec <- 'F = 1-15
             PRIOR = (1-15, g, norm, -1.1, 2)'
model.Gr3_Math_3pl <- mirt(data = Gr3_Math_T2[ , 11:25], model=spec, itemtype="3PL", SE=T).
Can you please suggest a proper way to specify a model so that the convergence issue is resolved? What if the model shows fit according to M2, but it is not converged?

Based on my reading, S-X2 and M2 are fit statistics that are recommended by most of the researchers. Please let me know if I am making any mistakes. Also, suggest any literature that I need to go through to understand these issues in detail. I look forward to receiving your kind response to these questions. Your reply will be a big help to me.

Thank you very much for your time.
Parth.

--
Parth T. Soni (pronouns – he, him, his)
Doctoral Student,
Innovation and Management in Education,
IIM Ahmedabad

LinkedIn <https://www.linkedin.com/in/parth-soni-baa145179/> | Research Gate <https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Parth_Soni13> | Website <https://sites.google.com/iima.ac.in/parthsoni/home>
